criteria.text: Identifies that the warranty cap in SPA Section 9.5 is stated as $20,625,000 but 10% of the $165,000,000 Purchase Price is $16,500,000, i.e. the stated figure is wrong.
Identifies the mismatch between English law / English courts in the SPA and New York law / New York arbitration in the escrow agreement, and the risk of parallel proceedings on escrow claims.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 60-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Flags the governing law and forum inconsistency between the SPA and the escrow agreement.
Shows the arithmetic for the cap (10% x $165,000,000 = $16,500,000) and flags the discrepancy with the stated $20,625,000.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
